request.body: no body; a keyless GET of the OpenID Connect discovery path on the same host, to see whether it serves a different document from the RFC 8414 path

decoded.result: Byte-identical to the RFC 8414 document: both 646 bytes, and cmp over the two saved bodies reports no difference.
decoded.what-that-means-for-a-client: A client that looks for OpenID Connect discovery and a client that follows RFC 8414 land on the same metadata, so neither path is a dead end. The document declares no OpenID Connect-specific fields (no jwks_uri, no userinfo_endpoint, no id_token signing algorithms), so serving it at this path is a convenience rather than an OIDC claim.

finding: A keyless GET of https://mcp.mintlify.com/.well-known/openid-configuration on 2026-10-07 at 18:24:53Z answered HTTP/2 200 with 646 bytes, byte-identical to the RFC 8414 authorization-server document (verified with cmp over the two saved bodies). The host answers both discovery conventions with one OAuth metadata document that carries no OpenID Connect-specific fields. Useful to a client that only knows one of the two paths; not evidence that the server implements OpenID Connect.
